title: Ancient Greek Religion
summary: Ancient Greek religion was a polytheistic system of worship centered on the Olympian gods and countless local deities, heroes, and spirits. Unlike modern organized religions, it had no single sacred text, founding prophet, or central authority — belief and practice varied by city-state, and religious life was woven directly into civic, domestic, and agricultural life rather than kept separate from it.

key_aspects.title: Worship and sacrifice
key_aspects.description: Worship centered on maintaining good relations with the gods through prayer, votive offerings, and animal sacrifice performed at altars, usually located outside temples rather than inside them. A typical sacrifice involved burning the bones and fat for the gods while the meat was cooked and shared among worshippers — a practice that combined religious devotion with communal feasting.

key_aspects.title: Temples and priesthood
key_aspects.description: See the dedicated 'Temples and Sanctuaries' entry for how temples, priesthood, and sacred precincts actually functioned.

key_aspects.title: Oracles and divination
key_aspects.description: See the dedicated 'Oracles and Divination' entry, covering Delphi, Dodona, and other forms of Greek prophecy.

key_aspects.title: Festivals
key_aspects.description: See the dedicated 'Religious Festivals' entry for the Panathenaea, the Eleusinian Mysteries, the City Dionysia, the Olympic Games, and the Thesmophoria.

key_aspects.title: Household and local worship
key_aspects.description: Alongside the major Olympian cults, everyday religious life included household deities like Hestia (goddess of the hearth), local heroes worshipped as protective figures for a particular city or region, and minor nature spirits — see 'Minor Deities, Daimones & Mythical Creatures' for more on nymphs and similar beings.

key_aspects.title: Mystery cults and the afterlife
key_aspects.description: Mystery cults such as the Eleusinian Mysteries and Orphic traditions offered initiates hope of a better fate after death — see the dedicated 'Death and the Afterlife' entry for how this fit into broader Greek beliefs about the Underworld.

key_aspects.title: Philosophy and religion
key_aspects.description: See the dedicated 'Greek Philosophy and Religion' entry for Pythagoreanism, Orphism, Stoicism, and the late-antique Neoplatonist and theurgic traditions.
